newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes firm as soybean market rallies.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes firm as soybean market rallies.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firm on gains in soybeans with weather outlooks giving the market some support, traders said.
Soybeans and corn jointly gained on ideas each market was oversold Wednesday and were due for a correction, they said.

Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for below normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation through most of the U.S. Midwest from September 10 through September 14.
Traders said the crop needs warm and damp weather rather than cool and dry.
Midday weather outlooks trimmed the chances of rainfall soon in the eastern U.S. corn growing region.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 52,000 contracts, down from 57,115 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, The Chicago Corp sold 500 December, $3.40 puts, Smith Barney sold 400 March $3.20 puts and bought 400 March $3.80 calls, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, down from 18,321 Wednesday.
Corn futures closed 3/4 to four cents per bushel higher, with September up 3-1/2 at $3.62-1/4.
